title: मौसी किसी से नहीं मिलतीं
logline: Kiran gives Mausi the all-clear with the groom wide awake beside her, then tells him what the other answer would have done. They drive to the bureau at dawn as two thieves who married each other, and inside Mausi, delighted with her new son-in-law, takes Kiran's left wrist to strip the chooda for tomorrow's bride, an arm's length from the man hunting the scar beneath it.
language_note: Hinglish: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script, in the same line.
script_note: Hinglish: Hindi in Devanagari, English words in Latin script

characters.name: किरण (Kiran)
characters.role: LEAD. The bureau's vanishing bride; tonight 'स्नेहा'. She has just given the all-clear with the groom awake.
characters.look: Indian woman, 27, about 5 ft 3, slight and wiry. Wheat-brown skin, oval face, straight dark brows, large kajal-lined eyes, closed watchful mouth. Low bun, centre parting with sindoor, two loose strands at the temples, small round red bindi, thin plain gold ring in the LEFT nostril, small gold studs, short black-bead mangalsutra. Block henna on both hands (solid disc in each palm, fingertips dipped). Red-and-ivory chooda on both forearms: a red cuff about 10 cm long with a pale ivory band at each end, starting just above the wrist bone. b1 to b3: plain sindoor-red matte saree with a thin plain gold border, red elbow-sleeved blouse, barefoot. From b5: plain ash-grey cotton salwar-kurta, three-quarter sleeves ending a hand's width above the chooda, grey dupatta over the left shoulder, flat black sandals. The scar on the LEFT outer forearm stays under the cuff in every shot.
characters.voice_note: Female, late 20s, alto with a dry edge. Small-city Madhya Pradesh Hindi with everyday English. In this episode she is Kiran, not 'Sneha': lower, flat, quick, तुम to Aditya, short sentences. With Mausi she sounds younger and says आप. Under pressure she gets quieter and more exact, never shrill. Lies come easily; true things come after a pause (l05).

characters.name: आदित्य (Aditya)
characters.role: The groom, a pharmacist, Mohit's elder brother. From b6 he plays a greedy thief who married a thief.
characters.look: Indian man, 33, about 6 ft, tall and narrow, slight stoop. Light-brown skin, long clean-shaven face, high forehead, calm deep-set eyes, thin mouth, short neat black hair parted on his left. Rimless rectangular glasses in every shot. Plain cream cotton-silk wedding kurta with band collar, sleeves folded back once, side pocket on the right; cream churidar. A 5 cm brass key on a doubled red cotton thread worn outside the kurta at mid-chest, in every shot. Plain steel watch, brown strap, left wrist. Barefoot in the bedroom, tan sandals outside.
characters.voice_note: Male, early 30s, light baritone, soft-spoken. Educated small-city Hindi in full sentences, तुम to Kiran, आप to Mausi, English nouns of his trade (dose, medical store). Even and unhurried. Playing the greedy husband (l11, l14, l15) he lets a little amusement in, but he never raises his voice and never swears.

characters.name: शकुन मौसी (Shakun Mausi)
characters.role: Runs the brides. Voice on a phone in b1 and b7; seen for the first time in this series in b9.
characters.look: Indian woman, 56, about 5 ft 2, broad and heavy-shouldered. Brown skin, round face, heavy-lidded shrewd eyes, paan-reddened lips, large round maroon bindi, small gold nose stud, grey-streaked black hair oiled into a tight bun. Starched bottle-green cotton saree with a narrow mustard border, mustard elbow-sleeved blouse, thin gold chain, rubber slippers. A steel ring of about eight keys hooked at her LEFT hip. A dozen plain green glass bangles on each wrist; forearms otherwise bare and unmarked.
characters.voice_note: Female, mid 50s, low, warm, grainy, a paan-chewer's unhurried mouth. Bundelkhand-side Hindi, Hindi-heavy, trade English only (line, set). An endearment in every second line. Laughs easily. On the phone she is fully voiced and clear, never a whisper. The colder the decision, the softer and slower (l19).

characters.name: बिल्लू (Billu)
characters.look: Indian man, 30, about 5 ft 7, wiry and restless. Brown skin, sharp jaw, patchy stubble, black hair gelled straight back. Faded blue denim jacket with sleeves pushed up over a black round-neck T-shirt, dark jeans, white sneakers gone grey. Wooden toothpick in the right corner of his mouth; car key on a plain steel ring hooked on his right index finger, except while driving (b7 to b9), when it is in the ignition. No weapon.
characters.voice_note: Male, about 30, light tenor, fast, a little nasal, talks round a toothpick. Small-town Bundelkhand street Hindi. Cocky and joking when he thinks he is in charge; goes loud for one line when surprised (l09), then looks to Mausi.

characters.name: छोटी (Chhoti)
characters.role: The next bride in training. Her first wedding is tomorrow (day 3). An adult woman.
characters.look: Adult woman, 19, about 5 ft 1, slight, light-brown skin, wide curious eyes. One long black braid over her right shoulder. Plain mustard-yellow cotton kurta with short sleeves, white salwar, a plain dupatta, rubber slippers. Two thin green glass bangles on the right wrist; left wrist bare; both forearms plainly unmarked. A phone in a plain pink cover in her right hand. Henna half done in Kiran's block style: LEFT palm disc and fingertips done, RIGHT hand bare. Nothing about her reads as a child (D-007 direction 14).
characters.voice_note: Female, 19, a young woman's voice, not a child's: bright, quick, a giggle in the breath. Small-town Hindi with a phone's English (ready). Calls Kiran दीदी.

characters.name: लड़के (The boys)
characters.role: Billu's two helpers. Silent. Seen only in b2 and not again in this branch.
characters.look: Never a face. Two backlit shapes from behind on a motorbike: one heavy-set, shaved head, maroon track jacket; one thin, checked shirt, cloth cap. Heads turned away or in shadow.

location: Five places, one night into one dawn: the bridal bedroom of the rented house (b1, b3, b5); the empty lane below with Billu's white sedan under one sodium streetlight (b2); the narrow stairwell and front door (b6); Billu's car on an empty highway at dawn, then stopped at a grey steel shutter (b7 to b9); the front room of Shubh Lagan Marriage Bureau and Beauty Parlour, shut to customers, shutter up, daylight and tube light (b10, b11). No crowd anywhere; no readable text in any image.
time_of_day: Night 1, 2:00 am (b1 to b5) and 3:00 am (b6); day 2 dawn, about 5:00 to 5:40 am (b7 to b9); day 2 early morning, about 5:45 am (b10, b11).

beats.action: Opens inside the same breath that ended s1e02. Shot 1 (l01): extreme close-up of Kiran's mouth and lower face in the amber lamplight, red saree, the pallu fallen over her LEFT forearm (picture-right when she faces camera); the cuff is complete again. Shot 2 (l02): insert of her black phone in its plain dark-red cover face-up on the white sheet between them, on speaker, caller name 'मौसी' and 2:00 as overlays, a marigold petal on the sheet beside it. Silent after: two-shot across the bed, a room's width apart, the untouched steel glass on the stool between them, the steel dabba still in Aditya's hand. The call-ended tone; Aditya, glasses on, key on its red thread, lets out a breath and lowers his eyes: the check he expected, the answer he expected.

beats.action: One still, no line. Billu leans on the bonnet of the white sedan under the sodium streetlight, toothpick in, pocketing his phone with his right hand, the car key hooked on his index finger. Behind him, deeper in the empty lane, the two boys are backlit shapes from behind on the motorbike, heads turned away, its red tail light already moving off. The bike's engine kicks and recedes (sound). Billu is the only face.

Same room, same night. Shot 1 (l03): Kiran single, sitting on the bed's window side, her voice dropped into her own register, flat and quick. Shot 2 (l04): Aditya single, on the almirah side, lamp key light, very still. Shot 3 (l05): Kiran close; she gives the name after a breath. Shot 3b (l06): Aditya close, holding on her while she goes straight to business off his face: for the first time he owes her something. Silent after: Kiran close, waiting for his answer. Her left forearm stays under the pallu throughout.

beats.action: Dawn. Silent before: wide exterior, the old white sedan alone on an empty two-lane highway through flat fields, ground mist, blue-grey light; no face readable. Fixed seating: Billu drives front right, Kiran front left, Aditya in the back behind Kiran. Shot 2 (l13): the rear-view mirror with Billu's eyes, toothpick at the corner of the frame, lemon-and-chilli charm hanging below; he does not turn round. Shot 3 (l14): Aditya in the back seat, glasses, key, the faint smile of a greedy man; Billu's eyes in the mirror at frame edge. Shot 3b (l15): Kiran in profile in the front seat, eyes on the road, giving nothing away while he sells the lie she set up. Shot 4 (l16): Billu's LEFT hand holds his phone out on speaker over the gear lever toward Kiran, the marigold string on the dashboard behind it; Kiran in profile. He keeps holding it there through l19. Shot 5 (l17): Kiran single, close, Billu's phone held near her face at frame edge, 'मौसी' overlay on its screen. Shot 5b (l18): from the back seat, Kiran in profile leaning to the phone in Billu's left hand, Aditya's shoulder and glasses soft in the foreground. Shot 6 (l19): insert of the phone in Billu's left hand over the gear lever, the light going orange.

beats.action: No line. Two set-ups. (1) Insert: Kiran's LEFT hand loose in her lap on the grey kurta, eyes shut or pretending, the first red sun coming through the chooda; the full cuff covers the forearm. (2) From the back seat: in the foreground, soft, Aditya's long fingers sliding the creased print back into his right kurta pocket, its white edge the brightest thing in frame; in the background, sharp, Billu's eyes in the rear-view mirror following that edge into the pocket.

The car stopped at a grey roll-down steel shutter in low orange sun. Shot 1 (l20): exterior two-shot, Aditya at the open front-left door taking Kiran's LEFT hand, the bangle hand, to help her out, playing the husband for Billu; he uses her working name. Silent after, two set-ups: (1) insert, 2 s: his fingers closed over her cuff, the stack shifted a little under them, no skin showing above or below it; late in the set-up the shutter starts to rattle up (sound). (2) Reverse, low from the car door, 2.5 s: the shutter risen, Shakun Mausi standing in it, green saree, keys at her left hip, paan smile; in the soft foreground the two hands are apart: he has looked up and let go. Glimpse A ends on set-up (1), cut before the rattle starts, and must not use set-up (2).

Two faces per frame at most. Shot 1 (l21): two-shot, Mausi holding Kiran's face in both hands, Kiran first, her eyes dropping from Mausi's; Mausi's forearms are in frame, bare and unmarked under the green glass bangles. Shot 2 (l22): Mausi single at her desk, the red velvet box open in front of her (Billu's hand at frame edge setting it down, no face), laughing till she coughs. Shot 3 (l23): Chhoti single on the cot, pink phone in her right hand, LEFT hand held out flat, back up, fingertips dipped, the outer forearm bare and unmarked. Shot 4 (l24): Aditya close, his eyes going from one wrist to the other. Shot 5 (l25): Kiran and Aditya side by side near the shutter, his head turned to her, hers not to him.

sfx_notes: Bedroom bed (b1, b3, b5): a warm still night through the open window, crickets, one distant dog, the lamp's faint electrical hum. No ceiling-fan sound anywhere in this series' bedroom.
b1: Mausi through the phone speaker: light filter only, warm and fully clear; the bed ducks under l02. Call-ended tone, then Aditya's out-breath, close and dry.
b2: sodium-lamp buzz; motorbike engine kicks, revs once and recedes down the lane.
b5: paper crackle as the fold is pressed shut; cloth of the kurta pocket; brass padlock clack and the iron bolt drawn back.
b6: stairwell echo, bare-bulb hum; the iron-sheet front door creaks on its hinge before l09; velvet box hinge snap under l11.

b7 and b8: old sedan engine at steady highway speed, tyre hiss, open-window wind low; birds coming up in the fields. Mausi on Billu's phone speaker (l17, l19): light filter, fully voiced; duck the engine bed under l17 to l19.
b9: engine idling then off, car door clunk, then the steel shutter rattling up, loud and long, starting late in the hand insert and finishing on Mausi. Glimpse A cuts before the rattle starts.

b10 and b11: tube-light hum, a street waking far outside, Mausi's keys chinking at her hip as she moves, glass bangles. Mausi's laugh in l22 breaks into a short paan-smoker's cough. Keys and bangles still under l24 and l25; the whisper dry and close. Duck everything under l27 and l28 so the chooda line is fully clear. The episode cuts on one dry glass-bangle chink, with nothing under it.
music_note: No music under the 2 am call in b1. A single low string drone enters on 'मोहित' (l05) and holds under the rest of the bedroom. The road (b7 to b8) gets a slow plucked pulse over the drone, warm as the light turns orange; it stops dead with the shutter rattle in b9. Bureau: the drone only, very low, rising a little under l27 and l28 and cut hard on the final bangle chink. Instrumental, no melody line, no percussion hits.
ending_question: चूड़ा आदित्य के सामने उतर रहा है: क्या वो किरण की कलाई पर निशान देख लेगा, और देख लिया तो क्या करेगा?
writer_notes: Sources: content/series1/bible.json revision 2, beat_outlines.s1a01, read together with docs/decisions.md D-003, D-005, D-007 (governs where it differs), D-008, D-013 and D-014. Beat ids follow the bible's stable ids: b4 was cut in D-005 change 9 and is left as a gap, so b1, b2, b3, b5 to b11. Line ids run l01 to l28 with no gaps.

Locked lines are verbatim: l01 'हाँ मौसी, पी लिया।' is the episode's first line, spoken whole; l13 is Billu's locked line. Anchor lines kept: l02 (Mausi), l18 (D-005 change 7 default, cut to its first sentence because Mausi's l17 has already said 'पी लिया'), l19 ('ले आ', given a 'हम्म...' lead-in for Mausi's pause and an endearment), l24 to l25 ('रेखा?' / 'अभी नहीं।', with 'कहाँ है' added as a carrier), l27 (Mausi's chooda line, verbatim). D-007 advisory for b7 used in a shorter form at l16, so Billu has told Mausi before the drive.

Cover story (story_locks.cover_story_branch_A): set by one line, l06, and then played, not planned: the brass shown to Billu (l11), the pharmacist's offer and the half sachet that 'did not work' (l14, l15), Kiran's reason to Mausi (l18), Mausi laughing at the brass (l22) and taking him on as the powder-maker (l26).

Wrist (near misses 1 to 3 of branch A): b5, Kiran offers the routine and he orders the chooda kept on for the newly-wed act; b9, his fingers close on the cuff and he lets go when the shutter rises on Mausi; b11, Mausi starts the first ivory bangle off for Chhoti, answered in s1a02 b1. No line says how tight a chooda is, how hard it is to remove or how long it is worn (story_locks.chooda.dialogue_ban). No frame shows the scar. Sides needed by the story are written as the character's LEFT with the picture side where it matters (D-013 rule 3).
Aditya first hears 'किरण' from Billu at l09 and uses it himself at l20. Mausi says बेटा and मेरी बच्ची, never the name. Chhoti's wedding is day 3, so Mausi's 'कल' at l27 (day 2 morning) is correct.

Faces per frame: at most two sheet faces in any set-up (D-007 direction 16); b6, b7, b10 and b11 are written as singles, two-shots and inserts. The boys appear only in b2, from behind; Billu is the only face there. Mausi's first image is b9 set-up 2.

Length: about 893 dialogue characters with tags removed (hand count; the critic counted about 883 before this revision, which added about 3), under D-007's working measure of about 1,050. Not padded. Spoken targets 89.5 s, 20 speaker changes at 0.3 s = 6.0 s, silent seconds 22.4 s (b2 cut from 3.0 to 2.0 s for the hook); target_total_seconds 117.9. Gate 0b measured real eleven_v4 takes 20 to 60 per cent over target; on that measure the speech alone puts this episode at an estimated 136 to 172 s (89.5 s of speech times 1.2 to 1.6, plus 28.4 s of gaps and silence). Length is settled in the edit from measured takes. If it runs over 135 s, trim in this order without losing a lock, a near miss or the pharmacist's offer in l15 (which l18 and l26 depend on): b5 silence 3.0 to 2.0 s; b8 cut to its second set-up, 4.5 to 2.5 s; b9 silence 4.5 to 3.5 s; then drop l16; then make l12 a laugh in the sound mix only.

Hinglish (S3 round 1): Kiran says 'code' (l03, paying off her s1e02 lie 'कोई code नहीं') and 'deal' (l10, which sets up 'सौदा' in l18); Aditya says 'medical store' and 'dose' (l15). Mausi keeps trade English only (line, set); Chhoti has 'ready'.

Staging (S3 round 1): no set-up holds more than one line where two lines would total over about 5 s at target. b3, b7 shot 3 and b7 shot 5 are split. In b3 the critic asked for the 1.2 s silence between l05 and l06; silent_position allows only before or after, so Aditya's hold plays over l06 instead (Shot 3b), and the silence after is on Kiran. In the car Billu's LEFT hand holds the phone on speaker over the gear lever from l16 to l19; the car key is in the ignition from b7 to b9.

Props: the mathri dabba (in Aditya's hand at the end of s1e02) is still in his hand in b1 and back in the maroon bag's side pocket in b5, so l21 pays it off. The red velvet box leaves the almirah in Aditya's left hand in b5 and is opened in b6. Kiran's phone is black in a plain dark-red cover (bible).

Tags: only tags already used in the proof scenes are written ([calm] [quietly] [sharply] [sighs] [chuckles] [laughs] [excited] [whispers]); none from the verify group. Every line is tagged, including the cliffhanger line l27 ([calm]). One true whisper (l24), with the bed held still under it. l11 is [chuckles], answered by Billu's [laughs] in l12. l09 is a cut-off on a full word ('रहा—'). Short turns that may need extra takes: l05 'मोहित।' (one word, after a sigh), l12, l25.

D-014: l19 has a deliberate pause on the ellipsis after 'हम्म'; the subtitle splits there if the take's pause is 300 ms or longer. Take check: 'हम्म' may garble on v4. If it does, use the fallback '[quietly] ठीक है... ले आ, बेटा।' (same tag, same target).
